I am a 50-year-old woman, and I have been farming these 7 mu in Quzhou for 20 years. I never went to school, but the land has taught me everything I need to know. My household has three people, and some of my family work off-farm, so I cannot waste labor on crops I do not trust. Cotton is what I know, and cotton is what my land is good for. I will plant all 7 mu with hybrid cotton — I have used guoxinmian before and it resists bollworm better than the old varieties, so I will stick with a hybrid seed. In late April, after the soil warms, I will rotary till the whole field and spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as a basal dressing before sowing. I have a well, so when the rain is not enough I will irrigate three times: once to help the seeds settle, once when the plants flower, and once when the bolls are forming. Pests are the biggest enemy here — aphids, bollworms, and spider mites come every year without fail — so I will spray pesticide about thirteen times through the season. I do not topdress much because the basal fertilizer usually holds, and my family’s off-farm income means I can buy the inputs I need without taking risks. If the weather treats me fairly, I expect to harvest around 550 kg of seed cotton per mu this year.
